findings.title: New awaitDns leg can push a fresh /boot past the client's 300 s abort
findings.detail: The fresh path now does `createInstance` (exec timeout 30s) → `platform.waitRunning(name, 240_000)` (line 403) → `platform.awaitDns(..., 120_000)` (line 404) before replying; the non-fresh path (line 421) does `platform.ensure` (which can include a 10s probe + 120s deploy + zombie-retry loops) plus another 120s `awaitDns`. Worst case is ~360–390s of server time. The client calls `bootInstance(conciergeAuth, 300_000, ...)` (client/src/App.tsx:142), and bootInstance uses `AbortSignal.timeout(timeoutMs)` (client/src/lib/concierge.ts), so the fetch is aborted at 300s while the machine is still legitimately booting. The catch then returns 'concierge stalled — boot gave up after 300s', `booted.ok === false`, and wakeCore's non-'no betterbase session' branch falls through to the legacy primary wake (`activeEnclave = ENCLAVE_URL; wakeInstance(...)`), pointing the user at the hardcoded `waddle` machine instead of their own. Note the `dns` result on line 404 is only logged — it drives no decision — so this 120s is pure added latency against the client budget. The previous code (waitRunning alone, 240s) left ~60s of headroom; this diff consumes it.
findings.recommendation: Bound the combined wait server-side (awaitDns budget = timeoutMs minus elapsed time, e.g. 120_000 - (Date.now() - started)), or raise/align the client's bootInstance timeout with the route's worst case.

findings.title: /boot/ready can never report ready on the docker backend, so every discovery boot ends in "gave up waiting"
findings.detail: Readiness is gated on `platform.statuses().get(instance) === "Running"`, but createPlatform's docker branch stubs the status feed: `statuses: () => Promise.resolve(new Map())` (concierge/src/platform.ts:91). `st` is therefore always undefined and the route returns 503 `{ready:false, why:"status"}` forever. On docker `/boot` always answers `status:"waking"` because `running = detail.startsWith("already running")` (index.ts:422) is false for ensure()'s `docker:<name> started` detail. The client's new gate (client/src/App.tsx:147-153) therefore always enters pollBootReady, burns its 90 attempts (~180s + fetch time) and reports "gave up waiting — try again" while the machine is up and /health answers. Before this diff the client polled /health directly, so docker wakes worked; the config-selected backend seam (CONCIERGE_BACKEND defaults to "docker") is now broken for any non-dev client.
findings.recommendation: Give the docker branch a real readiness answer — e.g. have it track `start` success (or have /boot/ready fall back to `platform.probe(url)` when the status map is empty) — instead of gating on a status feed the backend does not provide.

findings.title: DNS readiness gate fails open on any resolver error, letting the client query an unconfirmed machine name
findings.detail: dnsLive treats every resolve4 error except ENOTFOUND/ENODATA as 'DNS is live' (`return true` on EAI_AGAIN/ETIMEOUT/blocked), and awaitDns returns as soon as one dnsLive call is true. This is the exact check the new /boot/ready endpoint (concierge/src/index.ts:441-450) relies on to decide `ready: true`, and the client's new pollBootReady (client/src/lib/concierge.ts) then immediately polls the machine URL. The prod concierge config (config/concierge-tinfoil-config.yml) only allowlists api.tinfoil.sh and accounts.betterbase.dev on the `control` network, and the code comment itself concedes 'the runtime egress allowlist may not carry DNS'. In that environment, or on any single transient EAI_AGAIN/ETIMEOUT, dnsLive returns true with no retry, /boot/ready answers 200/ready, and the browser issues its first /health query against a machine name whose DNS record may not exist yet — reproducing the NXDOMAIN-poisoning the entire change was built to prevent (SOA negative TTL ~30min; the change's own comments cite Chrome-cached NXDOMAIN at 02:30Z). The gate that is meant to protect the client's resolver can therefore pass while the record is unresolved.
findings.recommendation: Distinguish transient/unknown resolver failures from a live record instead of returning true on the first non-ENOTFOUND error: keep retrying within the awaitDns budget on EAI_AGAIN/ETIMEOUT (and only report ready on a real successful resolve4), or return an explicit 'unknown' that /boot/ready surfaces distinctly rather than collapsing it into ready. If a blocked-DNS environment must degrade to status-only readiness, gate that behavior on an explicit config flag so the fail-open is intentional and observable, not the default for every transient error.

findings.title: New awaitDns/dnsLive DNS semantics ship with zero tests in a fully-tested module
findings.detail: The diff adds `dnsLive`/`awaitDns` (and the `probe` member) to the Platform seam, and `/boot` + `/boot/ready` now gate readiness on them. `concierge/src/platform.test.ts` pins virtually every other Platform method (`statuses`, `list`, `ensure`, `start`, `rest`, `waitRunning`, docker backend, timeout honesty) with explicit assertions, but nothing exercises `awaitDns`/`dnsLive`. The error-code branch is load-bearing and subtle: ENOTFOUND/ENODATA must mean "not yet" (keep polling) while any other resolver error (EAI_AGAIN/ETIMEOUT/blocked egress) is treated as "live" (true) so the Running-status signal carries. A regression that flipped this (e.g. treating all resolver errors as false) would make `/boot/ready` never turn ready behind an egress-blocked DNS, so every waking boot would fall through to "gave up waiting — try again" — the exact class this PR is trying to fix — with no test to catch it. The docker backend's `awaitDns: () => Promise.resolve(true)` short-circuit is likewise unverified.
findings.recommendation: Add platform.test.ts cases with an injected DNS resolver (or module mock) covering: ENOTFOUND→false, ENODATA→false, other error codes→true, a record that appears after N polls→true, and timeout→false; plus a docker-backend case asserting awaitDns resolves true without shelling out.

findings.title: pollBootReady's retry-on-throw branch is never exercised
findings.detail: `pollBootReady` documents two failure modes: a non-ok response and a thrown fetch/`authHeaders` error ("concierge hiccup — retry"). The two new tests only feed `ok: true` and `ok: false`; the `catch` branch that must continue retrying (rather than abort) is untested, as is `onTick` firing. A regression that let a thrown error escape would abort the wake instead of retrying, and no test would fail.
findings.recommendation: Add a case where the stub throws for the first N calls then returns ok, asserting pollBootReady keeps polling and eventually returns true, and a case asserting onTick is invoked per attempt.

findings.title: The fresh-path "retire" is only a memory forget: the adopt scan re-adds the retired name and rebind can hand it back
findings.detail: `users.forget(old)` drops the name from the in-memory known-set/map only. The recurring `scanUsers` (index.ts:701-709, once at boot and every POOL_SCAN_MS=5min) calls `users.adopt([...statuses.keys()])`, whose filter is shape-only (`re.test(name)`), so the retired machine — still Running on the platform — is re-added to `known` and becomes authorised again. After a concierge reboot the sub→name map is empty, so `users.rebind(sub)` falls back to scanning `known` and returns the FIRST prefix match in iteration order (adoption order = arbitrary platform-list order): it can return exactly the name the client watched die and already has NXDOMAIN cached for, defeating the whole point of the `fresh` flag. The retired instance is also never stopped (no platform.rest), so it keeps billing until its own idle row fires.
findings.recommendation: Keep retired names in a tombstone set that `adopt`/`rebind` exclude (or version the name with a generation), and reap the retired instance when fresh is requested.

findings.title: /boot/ready route and the /boot `fresh` retire path have no test coverage
findings.detail: The new `app.get('/boot/ready')` handler encodes several untested decisions: it rejects with 403 when `instance` is missing or fails `allowedInstance`, returns 503 `why:"status"` when the status feed is not 'Running' (including when `platform.statuses()` throws — the `.catch(() => new Map())` collapses a status-API failure into the same 503, so the client polls to exhaustion), and 503 `why:"dns"` when awaitDns fails. The `/boot` change that retires the user's old machine on `fresh:true` (`users.rebind`/`users.forget`) is also only tested at the `user-machines` unit level, not through the route. No concierge route-level test exists (grep for app.post/app.get/inject in *.test.ts returns nothing), so these branches are entirely unverified end-to-end.
findings.recommendation: Add a fastify `inject()` test for /boot/ready covering the 403 (missing/foreign instance), 503 status, 503 dns, and 200 ready paths with a stubbed platform, and a /boot test asserting `fresh:true` forgets the previous machine mapping.

findings.title: BootReadyResponse documents a /health leg that /boot/ready deliberately does not perform
findings.detail: The new SDK comment states "200 = the machine is Running AND its DNS resolves AND its /health answers (concierge-side, cache-free)", and the PLAN.md hunk repeats the same claim. The handler explicitly does the opposite: "NO /health probe leg: the concierge's egress cannot reach instance hosts" (concierge/src/index.ts:447-450), returning 200 on Running + DNS alone. Clients written against the documented contract would treat a 200 as proof the agent answers /health and skip their own probe; today 200 only means the name is resolvable.
findings.recommendation: Correct the BootReadyResponse and PLAN.md wording to what is actually checked (Running + DNS live), or add the probe leg the docs promise.
